title: Implement speculative-decode routing with acceptance scoring and graceful fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Add runtime support for speculative decoding that routes prefill+decode requests to fast model variants, measures an acceptance signal, and falls back to high-quality variants only when necessary. The feature should reduce median latency and token cost for chat/generation workloads while keeping quality regressions below a configurable tolerance. This ticket covers routing policy, acceptance score computation, integration with prefill vs decode scheduling, and a deterministic fallback mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: Speculative routing path implemented in serving runtime with config flag speculative.enabled=true
Acceptance score produced per-response and recorded to metrics store (histograms for acceptance-rate and per-token latency delta)
End-to-end fallback implemented: if acceptance fails, decode falls back to baseline model and preserves output ordering for requesters
Automated canary shows >=15% median latency reduction on chat benchmark with <2% reduction in BLEU/ROUGE-like eval on our validation prompt set
Kernel-selection path remains compatible: speculative variants can use different kernel profiles without breaking decode fallback
Prefill/Decode scheduler avoids wasted prefill compute when speculative acceptance is unlikely (adaptive short-circuiting)
E2E tests exist in CI covering cold-start, KV-cache warm-up, and race conditions between speculative and fallback decodes
notes: Background: We already have smaller quantized variants that are ~3x faster but occasionally degrade on long-range coherence. Speculative decode should route to these when latency is prioritized.

Design decision: Use a lightweight acceptance scorer that combines cross-model n-gram overlap heuristic, average token log-prob delta, and a small learned binary classifier that runs on CPU. Trade-off: classifier adds 1-3ms but reduces false acceptance significantly.
Routing policy: allow per-route policy config: mode={always-on, traffic-quantile, adaptive-cost}, threshold in [0,1], and model-hierarchy list [fast-quant, baseline, fallback-large].

Prefill scheduling: when speculative path selected, prefill executes on fast model variant; we record KV cache diffs and checkpoint keys to enable reuse if falling back, avoiding full re-prefill when possible.

Kernel selection interaction: runtime must keep kernel profiles for both speculative and baseline variants. When fallback occurs mid-decode, we re-select kernels for baseline; ensure no stale fused-kernel state is used across variants.

Fallback modes: synchronous fallback (blocking until baseline returns) and background upgrade (return speculative result immediately but start baseline in background and notify if baseline significantly better). Default is synchronous for deterministic APIs; background mode is opt-in for experimental routes.

Metrics: expose acceptance_rate, accepted_latency_vs_baseline, fallback_rate, wasted_prefill_seconds, decode_recompute_ratio. Wire these to console dashboards and alerts if fallback_rate > 5% for production routes.
Cost accounting: bill speculative and baseline token compute separately; show combined effective token cost in per-route analytics.
Open question: threshold calibration cadence. Proposal: daily automatic recalibration using rolling 7-day eval prompts and user-defined quality SLOs.
Performance target: speculative path should not increase 95th percentile latency beyond baseline SLAs for affected routes. If it does, feature toggles must disable per-route.
Relevant prior tickets: ENG-8732 and ENG-9014 informed acceptance metric design but do not duplicate routing/fallback semantics implemented here.
implementation_plan: Week 1: infra - add speculative.enabled flag, model-hierarchy config, and basic routing into runtime router
Week 2: acceptance - implement CPU acceptance scorer, instrument metrics and logs, add unit tests for scorer outputs
Week 3: prefill - KV-cache checkpointing and reuse hooks; implement lightweight prefill short-circuit logic
Week 4: fallback - implement synchronous fallback control-flow and background upgrade path; ensure ordering guarantees and backpressure handling
Week 5: kernels - ensure kernel-profile lookup supports dual-variant execution; add integration tests for kernel-selection when swapping variants
Week 6: canary & metrics - run canary on internal prod shadow routes, collect acceptance_rate and quality deltas, iterate on thresholds
Post-canary: roll out opt-in to selected customers and add console dashboards and SLA gates
testing_plan: Unit tests for acceptance scorer logic and thresholding rules
Integration test simulating speculative success and forced fallback with KV-cache reuse validated
Load test to measure wasted_prefill_seconds and overall cost impact under bursty traffic
Quality regression test run daily on our validation prompts comparing speculative vs baseline generations
Chaos test: kill speculative model container mid-decode to validate fallback resiliency and ordering guarantees
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind org-level flag; default off for existing customers
Internal canary: 5% of internal traffic for two weeks, monitor fallback_rate and quality metrics
Gradual rollout: increase by 10% per week for non-critical routes if metrics stable
Customer opt-in via console per-route toggle and a clear warning about experimental quality trade-offs
Rollback: immediate global disable if fallback_rate > 20% or if customer complaints escalate

2025-02-25 | Marco Nguyen: Implemented KV-cache checkpointing. Observed ~40% of fallback cases can reuse cache and avoid full prefill; added metric decode_recompute_ratio.
